importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types (compact 4×4 kiosk vs larger 6×6 double-guard cabin), colour finishes, window configurations, and cladding types. Buyers scan listing tiles to confirm visual fit and cabin type before reading any text — wrong appearance causes immediate skip.

Cabin size is a hard gate constraint (gate footprint determines which cabin fits). Sheet thickness and insulation type define the quality tier and price band. Listings without these specs cannot be shortlisted.

Price varies substantially with cabin size and insulation tier — buyers compare prices only after confirming spec equivalence. Indian buyers are price-aggressive but final price is negotiated; listed price is a budget entry point.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — market is fragmented across regional MS fabricators; buyers search by size and spec, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Fabricator credibility (delivery reliability, installation support, after-sales service) matters during vendor selection, but no recognised brands exist — company ranks after spec and price in the buyer journey.

importance_ranking.unit_note: A minority of sellers quote custom or large cabins per sq ft of floor area, but per piece is the dominant and universally understood convention for complete prefabricated cabin units.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — no buyer ever questions whether a complete prefabricated security cabin is sold per piece. Showing unit adds no information.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — non-interchangeable across gate footprint constraints, with a very large price delta between the smallest (4×4 ft) and largest (10×8 ft) configurations.
Defines the quality and comfort tier — No Insulation vs PUF or Rockwool carries a significant price delta and determines suitability for climate-exposed or premium deployments.

missing_important_specs.why_important: MS vs GI (galvanised iron) is a primary material variant with different corrosion resistance, longevity, and price — buyers in coastal or high-humidity deployments specifically require GI, and the existing 'Structure Material' spec only captures Steel Frame vs MS Frame (effectively the same value).

MS corrugated sheet, colour-coated sheet, and ACP cladding are distinct product variants with meaningfully different aesthetics, durability, and price points — buyers for premium residential or commercial deployments specifically request ACP or colour-coated finishes.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Primary dimension defining the cabin size class — sellers need length to determine which standard configuration applies and to quote accurately.
Second dimension completing the floor footprint — together with length, fully defines the floor area and price tier for the seller's response.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot quote accurately without knowing whether the buyer needs an insulated cabin — insulation type changes material cost significantly and determines product eligibility for climate-exposed deployments.
